provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of jss two work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall basic art concepts from JSS 2.
The students should be able to identify different music genres studied in JSS 2.
The students should be able to demonstrate simple drama techniques learned previously.

Introduction:
Today we will revise what we learned in JSS 2 to prepare for new topics. This revision will help us remember important concepts before we move forward.

Content:
We will review basic art elements like line, shape, form, space and texture. For music, we will revisit rhythm, tempo and dynamics. In drama, we will practice character development and simple stage movements. We will use examples from Nigerian culture like Adire fabric patterns, Yoruba drumming and traditional masquerade performances.

Class activity:
Students will create quick drawings of Nigerian cultural symbols and identify the music genre of short audio clips.

Evaluation questions:
Name three elements of art.
What is the difference between fast and slow tempo?
Describe one Nigerian traditional music instrument.

Summary:
Today's revision has refreshed our knowledge of basic art, music and drama concepts from JSS 2.

topics.title: Art: colour theory deep
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the primary, secondary and tertiary colours.
The students should be able to identify different colour schemes.
The students should be able to create a painting using a specific colour scheme.

Introduction:
We have learned basic colours before, today we will go deeper into colour theory. Understanding colours better will help us create more beautiful artworks.

Content:
Primary colours are red, yellow and blue. Secondary colours are made by mixing two primary colours: orange, green and purple. Tertiary colours are made by mixing a primary with a secondary colour. Colour schemes include monochromatic, analogous, complementary and triadic. For example, the Nigerian flag uses complementary colours of green and white.

Class activity:
Students will choose a colour scheme and paint a simple scene using only those colours, perhaps a market scene with fruits.

Evaluation questions:
What are the three primary colours?
Name two colour schemes.
How do you make the colour orange?

Summary:
Today we have deepened our understanding of colour theory and different colour schemes.

topics.title: Art: composition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define composition in art.
The students should be able to identify balanced and unbalanced compositions.
The students should be able to create a balanced composition in their artwork.

Introduction:
Good art is not just about the objects you draw, but how you arrange them. Today we will learn about composition to make our artworks more pleasing.

Content:
Composition is how elements are arranged in an artwork. Balance can be symmetrical, like the National Assembly building in Abuja, or asymmetrical, like a busy Lagos market scene. Focus point is where the viewer's eye goes first. We use techniques like rule of thirds, leading lines and framing to create good composition.

Class activity:
Students will compose a scene of a local market, ensuring balance and clear focus point.

Evaluation questions:
What is composition in art?
Name two types of balance.
Where should the focus point be in a composition?

Summary:
Today we have learned how to create balanced compositions in our artworks.

topics.title: Music: theory basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different musical keys.
The students should be able to explain the difference between major and minor scales.
The students should be able notate simple melodies using standard notation.

Introduction:
Music has rules that help us understand and create it. Today we will learn basic music theory to read and write music properly.

Content:
Keys are groups of notes that form the basis of a piece of music. The most common key in Nigerian folk music is the pentatonic scale, which uses five notes. Major keys sound happy, like Fela Kuti's music, while minor keys sound sad, like some traditional mourning songs. Notation uses symbols to represent pitch, duration and rhythm.

Class activity:
Students will practice writing simple melodies in both major and minor keys using staff paper.

Evaluation questions:
What is the difference between major and minor scales?
Name two common musical keys.
What does a music notation tell us?

Summary:
Today we have learned basic music theory including keys, scales and notation.

topics.title: Music: Nigerian music history
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to trace the evolution of Nigerian music.
The students should be able to identify key Nigerian musicians and their contributions.
The students should be able to differentiate between various Nigerian music genres.

Introduction:
Nigerian music has a rich history that has influenced music worldwide. Today we will explore how Nigerian music has evolved from traditional to modern forms.

Content:
Traditional Nigerian music includes genres like Juju, Fuji and Highlife. In the 1970s, Fela Kuti created Afrobeat, blending traditional rhythms with jazz and funk. Today, artists like Burna Boy and Wizkid have taken Nigerian music globally with Afrobeats and Afropop. Each genre has unique characteristics and cultural significance.

Class activity:
Students will listen to samples of different Nigerian genres and discuss their similarities and differences.

Evaluation questions:
Who created Afrobeat music?
Name two traditional Nigerian music genres.
How has modern Nigerian music evolved from traditional forms?

Summary:
Today we have explored the rich history and evolution of Nigerian music.

topics.title: Art: print and design
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the process of lino printing.
The students should be able to create a simple lino print design.
The students should be able to identify different printmaking techniques.

Introduction:
Printmaking is an important art form that allows us to create multiple copies of a design. Today we will learn about lino printing, a popular printmaking technique.

Content:
Lino printing involves carving a design into a block of linoleum, applying ink, and pressing it onto paper or fabric. The carved areas remain white while the uncarved areas pick up the ink. Common designs in Nigerian printmaking include Adire patterns and geometric motifs inspired by traditional architecture.

Class activity:
Students will carve a simple design into a lino block and create prints using different colors.

Evaluation questions:
What materials are needed for lino printing?
What is the difference between the carved and uncarved areas in lino printing?
Name one Nigerian traditional print design.

Summary:
Today we have learned about lino printing and created our own print designs.

topics.title: Drama: theatre history
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify key periods in Nigerian theatre history.
The students should be able to explain the significance of Nigerian traditional theatre.
The students should be able to perform a short scene using Nigerian theatre techniques.

Introduction:
Theatre has deep roots in Nigerian culture, used for storytelling and community events. Today we will explore the history of Nigerian theatre and its evolution.

Content:
Traditional Nigerian theatre includes masquerade performances, like the Eyo festival in Lagos, and storytelling sessions under the moonlight. In the colonial era, theatre was used for education and protest. Post-independence, playwrights like Wole Soyinka and Ola Rotimi created works that blended traditional and modern theatre forms.

Class activity:
Students will perform short scenes using techniques from different Nigerian theatre traditions.

Evaluation questions:
What is the significance of masquerade performances in Nigerian theatre?
Name two Nigerian playwrights and their contributions.
How has Nigerian theatre evolved from traditional to modern forms?

Summary:
Today we have explored the rich history of Nigerian theatre and its cultural significance.

topics.title: Art: digital art
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify basic digital art tools and software.
The students should be able to create a simple digital artwork using appropriate tools.
The students should be able to explain the advantages of digital art over traditional art.

Introduction:
Digital art is becoming increasingly important in our modern world. Today we will learn about digital art tools and create our own digital artworks.

Content:
Digital art uses technology to create art. Common tools include drawing tablets like Wacom, and software like Adobe Photoshop and Procreate. Digital art allows for easy editing, undo mistakes, and working with layers. Nigerian artists use digital art to create modern interpretations of traditional motifs, like Adire patterns or Benin bronze designs.

Class activity:
Students will use a digital art app to create a piece that combines traditional Nigerian motifs with modern elements.

Evaluation questions:
Name two digital art tools or software.
What are the advantages of digital art over traditional art?
How can Nigerian culture be represented in digital art?

Summary:
Today we have learned about digital art tools and created our own digital artworks.

topics.title: Music: production basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify basic music production equipment.
The students should be able to explain the process of mixing and mastering.
The students should be able to create a simple beat using basic production techniques.

Introduction:
Music production is the process of creating and preparing music for release. Today we will learn about the basics of music production and create our own simple beats.

Content:
Basic music production equipment includes a computer, Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) like FL Studio or Logic Pro, headphones and MIDI controllers. The production process involves composing, arranging, recording, mixing and mastering. Nigerian music producers often blend traditional rhythms with modern electronic elements to create unique sounds.

Class activity:
Students will use a simple DAW to create a short beat incorporating Nigerian rhythmic patterns.

Evaluation questions:
What equipment is needed for basic music production?
What is the difference between mixing and mastering?
How do Nigerian music producers blend traditional and modern elements?

Summary:
Today we have learned about music production basics and created our own simple beats.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer past BECE questions accurately.
The students should be able to identify areas of weakness in their knowledge.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper exam techniques.

Introduction:
As we approach the end of term, we need to prepare for our exams. Today we will practice with past BECE questions to improve our exam skills.

Content:
We will review key topics from this term including colour theory, composition, music history, printmaking, theatre and digital art. We will practice answering questions in the format expected by BECE, with proper time management and clear explanations. Nigerian exam questions often ask for examples from local culture, so we will ensure our answers include relevant Nigerian examples.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to solve past BECE questions and present their answers to the class.

Evaluation questions:
Explain one concept learned this term with a Nigerian example.
What is the proper way to answer an exam question?
Name three topics we have covered this term.

Summary:
Today we have practiced with past BECE questions to prepare for our upcoming exams.
